title: "Simulated encode and recall covariance slopes"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Simulated encode and recall covariance slopes}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

This replaces an older example that used a removed dataset constructor and
presented task-main-effect evidence as evidence for interactions. The example
below uses synthetic scan-level inputs to illustrate the covariance workflow.
It does not recover latent neural signals or validate statistical inference.

```{r}
library(multiPPI)
set.seed(2024)
n <- 160L
runs <- rep(1:2, each = 80)
encode <- rep(c(rep(1, 8), rep(0, 8)), length.out = n)
recall <- 1 - encode
vividness <- recall * runif(n, 0.4, 1)
X <- cbind(intercept = 1, encode = encode, vividness = vividness)
Y <- matrix(rnorm(n * 6), nrow = n)
fit <- mppi_fit(Y, X, psych_idx = 2:3, runs = runs, scale = "cov")
length(fit$Delta)
head(mppi_evidence(fit)$per_column)
```

`fit$Delta` contains descriptive covariance-slope matrices. The evidence above
compares task-main-effect models of the response and is not evidence for
covariance modulation or a conventional PPI interaction. The legacy
covariance-resampling methods without a qualified null fail closed. For a
seed-based gPPI design and named condition contrast, see the conventional PPI
vignette.
